To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MF is biased in theory and impractical in practice, and that the WMF and the WCF are the pertinent sequence design criteria for the constant and nonconstant modulus complex-valued sequences, respectively.

the WMF and the WCF, based on the weighted correlation model, are more pertinent and tractable sequence design criteria in theory and practice, respectively, than their unweighted counterparts, the merit factor and the cross-correlation factor.

the MF is not a pertinent anti-multipath sequence design criterion for the constant amplitude sequences and the non-constant modulus sequences, the weighted MF is a more pertinent anti-multipathy design criterion for the former and the latter, and the weighted cross-correlational factor is a more pertinent MAI rejection design criterion in the context of CDMA systems with multipath propagation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the fundamental issues of how to accurately evaluate and design sequences with good anti-interference property in the context multipath propagation, which are of great importance to the design of sonar, radar and CDMA systems.
a new approach of sequence design criteria and a new class of sequences with better anti-multiple-access interference property for CDMA systems.
shedding new light on the design of binary sequences for multipath environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MF is an inaccurate and biased performance evaluation metric and a nonpertinent sequence design criterion, while the WMF and WCF are accurate and pertinent sequence design criteria in the contexts of single-user and multiple-access systems, respectively.

the MF should not be used as a sequence design metric for the binary sequences of practical interests, whereas the WCF is the most pertinent metric for the CDMA sequence sets of practical interests in the context of the multipath channel.

the MF and the WCF are the best and the worst sequence design criteria, respectively, for the anti-multipath and the MAI rejection property of a binary sequence or a sequence set in the presence of multipath.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed WMF and WCF are more pertinent sequence design criteria for anti-multipath and anti-multipath multiple-access applications than the current standard MF and the standard cross-correlation factor.
the MF is not a pertinent design criterion for binary sequence design for multipath channels and that the WMF is the pertinent criterion for binary sequence set design for the multipath CDMA systems.
the proposed WCF and WMF are more appropriate and pertinent sequence design criteria for CDMA and direct sequence spread spectrum (DS-SS) systems, respectively, than the MF.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MF is not a pertinent design criterion for most practical sequences and, more importantly for the CDMA applications, the cross-correlation factor should be redefined as the WCF for a more accurate and practical evaluation of the MAI rejection property in multipath channels.
the MF is not a pertinent anti-multipath sequence design criterion in practical applications and should be replaced by the WMF in the future.
the MF and the cross-correlation factor should not be used as the sequence design criteria for sonar, radars, and communication systems in practice.
